Ravi Mehta: Quick RFC follow-up: propose "signal contracts" + an enforceable actuator API + a flight-recorder audit trail for every automated fallback. Short discussion.
Lina Chen: Nice. Signal contract = typed envelope (channel, severity, score, expires_at, evidence_url)?
Ravi Mehta: Yes. Actuator only consumes envelopes and a per-service policy. That keeps actuators simple and auditable.
Omar White: How do we avoid noisy spikes causing flip-flop? Need damping + min-stable window in policy.
Jules Park: Also add per-service safety budget (max_auto_rollbacks/day) and a cooldown multiplier when budget low.
Lina Chen: Flight recorder idea: persist raw envelope + sampled metric slices and the final action taken, with provenance tags. Retain 90 days by default.
Ravi Mehta: For speed, local actuators cache signed envelopes TTL'd; emergency actions allowed locally (reversible only) while awaiting central confirmation.
Omar White: Enforcement: reversible actions (divert, reduce-weight) immediate; irreversible (model switch) require central signed approval and a brief staging window.
Jules Park: Transport: gRPC push with TLS + JWT. Fallback to signed HTTP webhook for infra without gRPC.
deploy-bot: deploy: canary started for search-v2 cohort=4% at 2026-03-22T09:40Z :rocket:
Ravi Mehta: Action items: Lina -> envelope proto + examples; Omar -> local cache TTL and cooldown logic; Jules -> safety budget schema. I'll sketch the flight recorder proto and link to RFC.
